Resync.description: Re-query GitHub for your organizations and installations. Offered on Home only, because Resync/Home is the sole grant -- actions attach by RIGHT, not by declaration, and this file is evaluated against every type. showedOn 'detail' puts it in the Home page's own action bar, beside Back, which is where the accounts grid it refreshes actually is. selectionRule '=0' because it acts on the caller, not on rows: a parentless, selectionless action is legal. refreshOnCompleted is false because ResyncAction emits its own client operations -- it refreshes the accounts query AND patches the two count attributes, which a blanket refresh does not do; leaving both on simply ran the query twice. NOTE: this file is a flat map of action name to definition, so a '_comment' key is not a comment, it is an action that fails to deserialize.

DeleteData.description: Erases a disconnected repository and every commit, build and coverage document under it. Offered on Repository only, because DeleteData/Repository is the sole grant. The right is granted to every signed-in user because rights here are group-level and there is no group per GitHub owner -- so the right decides who is OFFERED this, and DeleteDataAction decides who may run it: the caller must manage the owner AND the repository must be disconnected. confirmation because it is irreversible. selectionRule '=0' because it acts on the repository whose page it is on, through args.Parent, not on selected rows. refreshOnCompleted is false because the deletion is asynchronous and runs in chunks: a refresh re-fetches an object that is still there and looks exactly like the action having done nothing, which is precisely how this button read while its queue was dead. DeleteDataAction instead notifies and navigates to the owner's page.

SyncColumns.description: Re-reads this board's Status field from GitHub and replaces its cached columns. It exists because NOTHING tells this app when a column changes: the Projects V2 webhook events are organization-scoped (a user-account installation receives none) and, measured, renaming a Status option emits no event for either owner type -- so the cache is corrected only by the nightly reconciliation or by this button, and until then a rule whose target column was deleted stays valid and silently never fires. Offered on GitHubProject only, because SyncColumns/GitHubProject is the sole grant -- actions attach by RIGHT, not by declaration, and this file is evaluated against every type. showedOn 'detail' puts it on the board's own action bar, next to the columns it refreshes. selectionRule '=0' because it acts on the board whose page it is on via args.Parent, not on selected rows. refreshOnCompleted is false because the action emits its own client operations -- it refreshes Columns, EventMappings and ColumnsSyncedAtUtc, and reports orphaned rules by name, none of which a blanket refresh does.

Revoke.description: Stops an upload token authenticating, by stamping RevokedAtUtc rather than deleting the document -- the record of which token existed, who created it and when it stopped working is the useful part of a credential history, which is also why security.json grants QueryReadEditNew/ApiToken with no Delete. Offered on ApiToken only, because Revoke/ApiToken is the sole grant: actions attach by RIGHT, not by declaration, and this file is evaluated against every type. The right is granted to every signed-in user because rights are group-level and there is no group per GitHub owner, so the right decides who is OFFERED this and RevokeTokenAction decides who may run it -- the caller must manage the account. confirmation because a revoked token cannot be un-revoked. selectionRule '=0' because it acts on the token whose page it is on, through args.Parent. refreshOnCompleted is false because the action emits its own RefreshQuery for the tokens grid; leaving it on simply ran the query twice.
